segments.text: Or-Rack
Work in progress
Observations:
I've covered the Or-Rack presence in Remosa elsewhere in this volume, so I'll spare the repetition. What I find worth examining here is what that presence doesn't produce.

Any one of them could break you in half without breaking a sweat, and yet a population of them has never leveraged that fact into anything resembling a political demand. They hold the garrisons, they fight in our wars, they do the hauling, the building, the labor that breaks lesser frames.
And yet the better-paid posts go to humans. Not by law, mind you. By habit. A law can be repealed. A habit just sits there until enough people get killed.

The reasons are less dramatic than you'd expect. They're a race with no homeland, and with no political movements to fall back on. Combine that with a continent where everyone is struggling, and the resulting calculation is simple: you keep your head down.

Who has the energy for protest these days? Who will they even protest against? Social norms, history? Please. They see themselves as more "Remosan" or "Haldrithian" than Or-Rack. If only the sentiment was shared by the older races as well.
The body modification gets a great deal of attention, and I'll detail it in the sections that follow. For now I'll note one thing.

While one might be tempted to view it through a lens of self-expression, spirituality, or even a reclamation of their cruel upbringing, I think the true mechanism at work here is more bleak. When self-sovereignty is taken from one, the response is often to pretend that it exists elsewhere.
Some become tyrants, and some turn inwards to shape the one thing they are capable of changing. You see where this is going. Never ever say that to an Or-Rack though.
Origins:

"What's a bio-forge anyway", you might ask. This ancient tech is more advanced than anything our researchers are capable of today, which is not the compliment it sounds like. The forges have been inoperable for centuries now, but there are records. It's a tough read.

Apparently they took living orcs and altered them into something different enough to earn a new name. Tougher, smarter, less prone to violence, and above all, built to be modified. The empire adjusted its Or-Racks for whatever the assignment demanded. Bad air, restructured lungs.

Unstable footing, reinforced joints. Couldn't maintain supply lines for armor, so they grafted plating straight into the shoulders. It was field maintenance, not culture. The culture came later, when the Or-Racks started doing it to themselves.

LUCKILY the forges are no longer needed. They were born with a "full package" and are definitely capable of reproducing naturally. You'll find them across most of the continent at this point, though like the Graith, there are more of them the closer you get to the empire's old core.

Still manning garrisons, work crews and civic life. A portion deserted during the Fracture Wars. Small groups that split off, moved into the spaces between holdings, and scraped together a living on their own terms. Hunter-gatherers, mostly.

These are the Or-Rack tribes, and they're still out there, small and scattered. Most Or-Racks will never join one, but you can be sure they're thinking about it after a rough day at work. Rarely a plan. Often a comfort.
Appearance:
Standing between two point one and two point four meters tall, the Or-Rack are mountains of dense, red-brown muscle that dominate whatever space they walk into. Their skin is textured and thick.

Short horns grow from the upper forehead, curved or stubbed, and male Or-Racks often have lower tusks from the jaw as well. Pointed ears, heavy brow, dark hair, usually braided or cut short. The women are leaner and their faces are a touch more human-like. Still intense-looking though.

They grow quicker than humans and die considerably sooner. A fourteen-year-old is a man, and fifty is a respectable age. The decline, when it comes, is fast. A few years of rapid deterioration and then they're gone. There's no long twilight, an Or-Rack is functional until they aren't.

By adolescence most have started modifying. The specifics are covered below, but visually: scarification, geometric tattooing cut deep into the hide, metal bolted along the arms or across the shoulders, bone studs set into the brow ridge. The unmodified ones tend to be children.
Clothing is unremarkable. They dress like whoever they live among, with a preference for showing what they've done to themselves. I'd call it tacky if it wasn't so essential to their upbringing.
Cultural Traits:

An Or-Rack handles on their own the way you'd cut your own hair, but anything structural requires a specialist: jaw reconstruction, spinal reinforcement, organ work. Every Or-Rack community of any size has one. They aren't paid for the service, not directly anyway.

The community honors them, keeps them fed and supplied, materials are gathered collectively, and in return their people get modified. In a garrison, the specialist is part of the unit. In a tribe, they work with what the land provides. Refusing is not illegal. It's worse.

An unmodified adult is either making a statement about how they see themselves relative to the rest of their people, and it's not a flattering one, or they're simply the Or-Rack equivalent of someone who shows up to a formal dinner in their nightclothes. The charitable reading is eccentric.
The usual one is less kind.

Or-Rack children are raised by their families in civic settings and by the tribe where one exists. A fourteen-year-old is expected to work, fight if necessary, and should probably already have their first significant modification. Or-Racks don't fuss over their young the way we tend to.

The child is taught what it needs to survive, and then it's expected to do so. They speak less than most and have little patience for talk that doesn't go anywhere. This extends to academics, philosophy, extended debate.
The exceptions to the rule tend to be either very good at what they do or a bit odd. Often both.

When the decline starts, an Or-Rack knows. The body they've spent their life shaping stops cooperating. Joints stiffen, modifications begin to reject, and the deterioration accelerates in a way that leaves little room for dignity.

Most Or-Racks settle what needs settling, say what needs to be said, and end it alone on their own terms. It is not discussed at length among Or-Racks, and it is not mourned the way humans mourn, but there is something. A father sitting with his children for an evening longer than usual.
A packed bag by the door. A fitting end, I guess, for a race defined by complete control over their bodies.
